title: Tighten an inline skate's ratchet cuff buckle: pump the lever until the cuff is snug, then fold it flat
instruction: Tighten the skate's cuff buckle until the cuff is snug, and leave the buckle closed.
context: Inline skating is a common pastime, and most recreational inline skates (here a Rollerblade Zetrablade: "Cuff buckle, 45° strap, laces") close the cuff with a ratchet buckle on a toothed ladder strap. Putting a skate on ends the same way: push the strap's tip into the buckle, pump the buckle's lever until the cuff is snug, fold the lever flat. K2's skate instructions: "When buckling up, push the ladder in as far as possible" and "'Ratchet' the ladder strap tight with the silver lever". Each swing of the lever toward the cuff draws the strap in a tooth or two against the cuff's rising pull; a catch holds it while the lever is lifted again; swung right open, the lever lets the strap go. The hand skill: hold a 55 mm lever and swing it through repeated arcs about its hinge as it stiffens, without opening it so far that it releases, then fold it flat. One arm does it: the skate stands in a wheel chock and needs no holding.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. One whole left inline skate, Rollerblade Zetrablade men's US 10 (black polypropylene shell and cuff, grey liner, 80 mm 82A wheels on a 30 cm frame), stands upright with its wheels between two pine rails (35 x 2 x 1.5 cm, at x 26.6 to 28.6 and 31.4 to 33.4, y -15 to 20) clamped to the table; its toe points to the robot's left (heel at y -11, toe at y 21), its outer side faces the robot. A foam boot shaper fills the boot. The cuff (12.4 x 10.8 cm, 15 to 28.5 cm high) is centred at x 30, y -3. Its cuff buckle (aluminium base on the cuff's outer side, y -5.5 to 0, face at x 24.2, 23.5 cm high) holds the black ladder strap (15 mm tall, 2.5 mm thick, 5 mm teeth) that wraps round the cuff's front from its inner side; the strap's tip is pushed 4.5 cm into the buckle, past its catch, the cuff loose. The red lever (55 x 18 x 6 mm, hinge pin at x 23.6, y -0.3) stands 90 degrees open, pointing at the robot. The skate stays in the chock; the lever and strap move. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The simulation reports how far the ladder strap has been drawn into the buckle, the lever's angle and each gripper's centre. Teeth: 5 mm teeth of the strap drawn in past the buckle's catch since the start (none once the strap has been let go). Scored on the state at the end: 0.1 per tooth, up to 0.6 at 6 teeth (30 mm, snug); 0.8 for 6 or more teeth with the lever folded flat (within 5 degrees, its tip within 5 mm of the buckle); 1.0 for that with both grippers 4 cm or more from the lever, the buckle and the strap's tip, and the lever and strap still for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a paint mark across the strap at the buckle's mouth at the start; at the end count the teeth past it (a ruler, 5 mm each), check the lever lies flat in a photo, and the grippers' clearance in the video.
reset_notes: Swing the lever right open so the strap slides out, push the strap's tip back into the buckle by hand until the paint mark is at the mouth (4.5 cm in, past the catch), and set the lever 90 degrees open, pointing at the robot, as in the screenshot. The skate stays in its chock. In the simulation each trial starts the simulator afresh (each inspect-robots run does).
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz. Skate, buckle, lever and strap at true size; the skate is held fixed in its chock. The cuff and boot shaper's give is a spring on the strap's slide (3 N plus 0.8 N/mm). The catch is a slide limit moved in tooth by tooth; the drive pawl is a rule: swinging the lever toward the cuff draws the strap 9.55 mm per radian, the strap's pull fed back as hinge friction. Only the strap's part at the buckle moves. Liner and laces are rigid.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers went to the skate, the left to the toe and laces, the right to the cuff's top, but neither took the lever, which stayed open); demo: 1.0
